text_fidelity_a:
Kid Galaxy RC Off Road Car. Claw Climber Tiger 4x4 Remote Control Vehicle, 2.4 GHz Wow! My toddler had been in a terrible mood all day, the sort of no good mood in which nothing satisfies and none of the toys or projects he was working on seem to come out right. Even a nap didn't cure it, but I'll tell you what did: this vehicle arriving in the mail. The presentation is awesome. You can see the face of the vehicle and the cool claws on the tires right from the get-go, and he immediately got excited. Though he is totally into trucks, construction vehicles, and things that go of all kinds, this got a higher level of excitement out of him because of how it was personified – it looks a little like Bowser from Super Mario Brothers, or has that same kind of appeal.

But, for a not quite three-year-old in a terrible mood, would he be able to work it? Though I've tested about 15 RC vehicles in the last year trying to find just the right one that he will be able to enjoy controlling, without going too fast, too slow, bottoming out on small obstacles, tipping over when driven over slopes, or being generally too complicated to run in some respect, only a few have passed the "I can do it myself" test. This is one of them.

The remote control is simple to understand and use, fits in small hands, and is lightweight and chunky to hold. Perfect for a toddler. There also isn't any pokey wire or metal antennae sticking out. I always wonder how companies justify giving that to a kid, given that they're going to be sprinting across the lawn not looking where they are going and liable to poke somebody's eye out, or their own if they fall.

I also really liked the speed level of this. I would've been happy if it were also a little slower to allow for better reaction time, but the speed was fast enough to be fun but not so fast that it's hard to control with childlike reflexes.

But the very best thing about it is those clawlike tires and the suspension. The claws are made of a softer rubberized plastic material, and the claws flap out with the centrifugal force of the tires movements, and retract in as needed. It's not something you can really control, they just do it themselves. Mine seem to have an error where one of the tires has the claws stuck inside for the most part and trying to pull them out on my own didn't work that well, they just retracted again and stayed retracted as soon as I started the vehicle again. No matter, it almost seems to help the car have better traction to have one back wheel that is essentially without claws.

The claws grip onto pretty much any surface, carpet, blankets, toys, rocks, lawn and woodchips, and thrust them out of the way so the car can off-road just about anywhere. We, perhaps unwisely, began our testing in the living room, where it climbed over a wide array of baby and toddler toys, turning upside down, then catching on a blanket and turning itself right back up before getting stuck in a ridiculously large mashup of garbage truck and Duplo bricks. It was exciting, impressive how it righted itself and went over such a wide variety of huge objects, and loads and loads of fun.

I also love the high suspension. Many other trucks, even ones with big monster tires such as from John Deere, ruin things by having a small plastic box on the underside of the vehicle which hangs downward and makes the vehicles bottom out on anything it hits. I don't know why this is such a "thing", but at least half of the RC vehicles we've gotten have this exact problem, even the off-road ones. This little truck does not suffer from that issue, and thus was able to go through a wide variety of terrains, and nothing seemed to stop it. It was going sideways on a pile of landscape trimmings, went upside down, righted itself, clawed its way all the way through the backyard and house with no issues.

The one complaint I have is not really a complaint, just a minor caution. It looks as though there is not really any way for sand and dirt and mud to work itself out of the holes in the tires were it to get truly filthy. We solve this problem by not taking it to the sand dunes or running it through sand or mud. We brought it to the playground that has woodchips and lawn, in the backyard that has woodchips and lawn, and discouraged our toddler from using it in the dusty vegetable beds in the backyard. No problem. However, if your vision is to bring it someplace truly dirty, I have no idea what the longevity would be and how nice the vehicle would look and work after prolonged running through such materials. It is off-road, but not necessarily all-terrain.

Overall, this is probably my favorite RC vehicle we've gotten yet. It is just so much fun, has great personality and really made an impression on our toddler, is easy to control, and doesn't have many of the issues that previous RC vehicles have suffered from. A thoughtfully designed toy all around, and fun for the whole family. I definitely don't feel too old for this, and my almost 3-year-old toddler isn't too young, so that's quite a range.
text_fidelity_b: Kid Galaxy RC Off Road Car. Claw Climber Tiger 4x4 Remote Control Vehicle, 2.4 GHz

Also, you need to keep a cover over the viewing area to help the veggies grow, so none of the roots are visible without an adult carefully removing and replacing the cover (which is a thin piece of plastic).  Our veggies sprouted quickly and well, and then promptly fizzled out.  You place 3 ropes through the dirt extending into the tray of water on the bottom, and these are supposed to wick all the needed water to the plants. At least here in Colorado, it is too dry and the plants couldn't get enough water.  They could however mold a little and then die.  The bottom holding tank of water turns into this muddy cistern that supports fruit flies amazingly well, and is easily knocked by an eager kid trying to see the plants.  The roots weren't particularly visible. This toy has been very disappointing overall, and now I have a hunk of styrofoam that I will have to pay to bring to our special recycling center.  Hoping that our garden reignites some excitement for growing things and the wonder of nature!

I like the number of musical instruments in this set, the fun little stand which has a lower spot for the music as well as a higher spot for holding Barbies music, and the music inspired outfits.

text_fidelity_a:
Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

text_fidelity_a:
Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009) This is a really cool and interesting game! I wasn't sure what to expect based on the box and description, but unlike other contraption based games I've played (like the classic "mouse trap" from my youth), this is more of a cooperative play game.
There are 4 strings that move a (clearly mission-impossible inspired) suspended character around the playing board, and it takes careful pulling and releasing each of them as a group effort to navigate properly, sort of like a marionette puppet meets a corporate team building activity. There are some things to do like remove security cameras and traps but the truth is, the real fun doesn't start until you open up the jewel cage.
Once the cage is open, there's a countdown (you can hear the spring noise whirring as soon as it opens) and the police car starts to slowly circle the board. If you make it to the getaway car with the jewel before the car makes it to block your path, you win! If, however, you take too long, the police car will spring into place and block your path. Hilarity ensues as players start to panic and lose their cool, and in the end, whether you make it or not, it felt exciting.
Things I like about the game:
- It is cooperative, not individual. So you don't "beat" another player, you work as a team to complete the task in time.
- The mechanical game board is unique and really fun to learn
- It does NOT require batteries! The board uses spring loaded timers where necessary, no electricity. This is cool in a decidedly analog way.
- People can walk over and see how it is played and join with very little instruction

Things I did not, however, like:
- The truth is, when playing with my kids, we sort of skipped the first part of the game and just jumped to the jewel part. The designers of this game tried to make it longer by adding disarming traps and pulling security cameras in particular order based on cards, but it felt tedious after a few rounds. Really the fun part is the end. The whirring police car gives a sense of danger and urgency that makes it fun.
- That little spy is suspended by strings that get tangled so quickly and easily. It feels like I sneeze and they are tangled. Out of the box, I had to spend time untwisting it before we played for the first time, so be careful.

That being said, the game is TON of fun for different ages and we actually had some guests come over who looked at it and wanted to play too (adults AND kids). They all asked where to to get it, so it might become a regular thing found in our neighborhood. I'd say it deserves 5 stars, it's been a while since a game sparked this much interest that wasn't on a screen.
text_fidelity_b: Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009)

text_fidelity_a:
K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy [[VIDEOID:5795137e2a23bd3d76a56d2b9446c889]] If you’re already familiar with K’Nex building sets, this K’NEX THRILL RIDES-REVOLUTION FERRIS WHEEL is a simple, fast build. The Ferris wheel is big, but it doesn’t require a lot of pieces. Also, much of the assembly involves building duplicate parts that combine to make the wheel and its swinging gondolas.

The set is recommended for age 7+, and that sounds reasonable (assuming that an adult provides some initial help with making the connections, and assists with lifting the wheel onto the axle). Each shape of piece is a different color, which detracts from the appearance of the finished Ferris wheel, but makes the construction simpler. There aren’t many “snowflake” connections, which I usually have to puzzle over to get the right orientation. (K’Nex pieces are much harder to work with than LEGO pieces.) The instructions are reasonably clear. This set took me about 5 hours to build (from opening the box to completion, working at a leisurely pace).

Unfortunately, the finished “thrill ride” isn’t very thrilling. Like a full-sized amusement park ride, the Ferris wheel doesn’t do much—it just goes around and around in a circle. Also, it does NOT have a variable speed control—you cannot start, stop, or speed up the wheel gradually (like a real ride). Although the motor has a single speed, it does run in forward and reverse directions. The motor is powered by two AA batteries (not included).

For the Ferris wheel to turn properly, one edge of the inner wheel track must be settled into the groove on the “gear wheel” attached to the motor. You can easily fiddle with the base to adjust things so that the track and groove always make good contact. Because it’s sort of boring and lacks a variable speed control, I rate this K’Nex Ferris Wheel kit at 4 stars (“I like it” on the official Amazon scale).
text_fidelity_b: K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy

VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park 5 stars for the toy itself. 0 stars for the directions - they are awful! The pictures are in blurry black and white, and the wording is confusing. It took me far too long to put together, but I was impressed by the finished product.

First of all - this is big! Look carefully at the specs on this toy to see if it will fit well (or dominate) your play space. The colors and designs are bright and cheerful, which I like. There are a few specific mechanical steps to make this work right with the car, and I worried that it would be too complicated for my 2yo granddaughter. (1) The arm needs to be clicked down into position, (2) you need to wind the car up the ramp (and the crank for that is tricky - if you let go just a little, it slides back to the bottom), then once the car slides down the ramp into the cradle you need to (3) release the arm for the catapult to launch down the second slide. Again - sounds complicated, right? But my granddaughter mastered it in no time! I was surprised and happy about that.

I was also very happy that she played with this over and over. She never seemed to get bored with it. The little car plays music and phrases as it goes along, and even when all the steps didn't go perfectly (ie: the car crashed), my granddaughter was amused. One quick note: some of the joints seem to come apart easily, and since toddlers are a little rough, we needed to keep an eye on this. Still, this will be a great toy that grows with our grandkids!
text_fidelity_b: VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park

text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy His torso isn't soft, but Elmo's arms and legs are, and that's what my dog went for as we attempted to unpack this toy from his tied down cardboard home. That's after getting through the mega cellophane tape that sealed the box. Your kids will need assistance in accessing the toy for play but they can press his stomach through the package opening to activate the Demo mode. Included in Elmo are AA demo batteries and I haven't opened the compartment to see what they look like or assess how they are different. Nowhere on the box are instructions, so first of all, know that you must switch from Demo to On by opening Elmo's bottom. I am happy to know that it's also possible to turn him off.

Elmo looks just like Elmo and when he talks or sings, his wide mouth moves. His voice is not very clear, but as kids play with him, they intuitively know what he will say. His songs are pleasant, directions are simple, and he doesn't provide negative reinforcement if his orders are not completed properly. This is important in keeping a child interested. Each of the 3 enclosed hard plastic hats has molded into the base a key which let's the toy know which activity to generate. This is very smart and it works well. Initially, it's not easy to get the key to settle, but I suspect that over time it will become more easy. I expect that younger children will need assistance in changing the hats.

The Playskool Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo is a fine toy that I'm confident can entertain and even educate many children. I am curious to know if he is produced in assorted languages as well as the English which ours speaks.
text_fidelity_b: Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy

The bags for each mini set are unnumbered, you’ll need to open all at the start. All of them except the bags of round 1x1 plates. The studs are meant to simulate dirt, and you don’t attach them to anything, simply pour them in the pots. I didn’t use the studs, the pots are really full and I couldn’t see the bases anyway.

The pieces mostly stay together on the succulents themselves. But some of the pieces are loose, especially the connections between succulent and pot. To build the sets, you assemble the various succulents and then attach them inside the pot. Most of the succulents clip into the base with bar pieces. Imagine a piece that looks like: —C. Sometimes those clips didn’t hold very well, so sticking a second succulent in was enough to dislodge the first.

Getting all the succulents inside each pot takes some finessing and patience. The finished sets are display pieces, not for play -- they are a bit delicate.

The instructions are usually easy to understand, though sometimes I did have to go back or flip forward to understand where a piece went. Some of the colors are off. For example, dark pink in the instructions are really orange pieces. The color differences made some of the sets harder than others, since I couldn’t always tell which piece to use.

I did like that the set include extra stamen options. Getting to choose my own flower colors among the options, or even mix them, was fun.

Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue) I love the old console games and I looked to this handheld to revisit some of the older games I remember enjoying several years ago. For the price this is a decent little console and I like it, though there is some room for improvement.

In the past, playing the older games required downloading a ROM and putting it into an emulator, and if you knew where to look for ROMs you could find hundreds of them, many familiar and even more that were very unfamiliar. I expected this little console to be something silimar to the old emulator, preloaded with old ROMs, and it seems to be fairly close to that. There are many games I recognize that are a lot fo fun to revisit, and there are a lot of games that are unfamiliar.

This console comes preloaded with several hundred games of varying types and quality. As mentioned there are quite a few that are familiar, but many that I never saw in an arcade. Some appear to be Asian releases that never were released here.

Navigation is a minor pain. If you want to play a game that is far down the list, you have to navigate there every time. There doesn't appear to be any memory for last games played.

Another minor disappointment is that several titles are listed more than once in the menu. This suggests to me that there are different versions, even if I can't tell what the differences are.

I'm thinking this is the same thing as the old emulators that can be found online and it just packaged in a handheld and preloaded with ROMs. That's fine by me, I like those old games. It would have been nice to provide better navigation, though, and maybe reduce the versions of each game to the latest or most bug-free? For the cost, it's a worthwhile system if you love those old games.
text_fidelity_b: Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue)

This can be played in your living room, bedroom, your yard, driveway, porch, at the beach -- just about anywhere inside or outside. I put this together in a few minutes. You set the outfit, rub the crayon over it, then color it. So, although the primary purpose of this toy is vanity, I like the creative and artistic aspect of it. My 6 year old daughter was thrilled when she saw it. The packaging leaves much to be desired. It is a clamshell package. I took it out, showed her how it worked, and set her to work on creating some outfits. There are 3 bottom plates (6 options), 3 top plates (6 options), and 3 head plates (6 options). All the plates fit inside a little drawer. It comes with one crayon to rub with an attachment so you don't have to get your fingers all messy and 4 colored pencils.

This is super cheap quality. The lid only closes (on the top) when you have the drawer pushed in. The plates themselves are not exactly even, they are a bit warped and don't lay flat. The drawing area is too small for a regular sheet of paper, but slightly larger than half a sheet of paper. You cut paper in half to use half sheets and they slide around a bit in the top area. Since the plates are a bit warped, you can't get a good rubbing of the pictures. (One skirt and top is polka dotted and not even half the dots will transfer to the paper.) The top is difficult to open. It also easily pops off on the opposite side that should not be opening. The eyes usually don't transfer to the rubbing either.

The colored pencils it comes with are pretty poor quality and not good color choices. (Brown, indigo, light pink, and yellow.) They don't have very much pigment in them and you're coloring on top of a rubbing, so you need much more vivid pencils than it comes with.

Within about 20 minutes of use, my 6 year old had already found the duct tape and taped the lid down. She likes the product and said other girls would like it too, just use duct tape.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Princess Design Activity Kit - 9 Double-Sided Plates, 4 Colored Pencils, Rubbing Crayon

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game I have two teenagers who spend a lot of time in their rooms. We have the occasional game night once or twice a month for some quality family time. This game has become my 16 year old daughter's absolute favorite game. She has even started having her friends over for game night. You roll the dice and whatever letter comes up is the letter that each word that you write has to start with for that round. You are given a card that tells you what to write. For example, the card may say "a color" for number 1. The die was rolled and it landed on the letter G for that round. So you have to write down a color that starts with G on your list. Now if you and anyone else write the same G word, neither of you get a point. You are trying to come up with the most original and creative word that fits the letter and the subject. It's usually hard to come up with all twelve words in a round when the timer is set! Brain Games - The Game - Based on the Emmy Nominated National Geographic Channel TV Series This game is rated for 3-6 players ages 14+. However, my boyfriend and I were able to play by just leaving out the head-to-head (challenge cards) for each category.

The object of the game is to be the first one to win a game piece in all four game categories. I love board games and so does my boyfriend, which is why I got this. At the beginning we found playing this game nearly impossible. Neither one of us watch TV (this is based on a TV series) nor have cable. Therefore, it took us a while to even understand what this was about and what many of the game cards were asking us to do. We kept asking ourselves “Are we really that stupid?” However, after playing for almost 2 hours, we were enlightened. Nevertheless, for the uninitiated, this game might be challenging and confusing the first time around. After that not so much because then one remembers how to solve most of the cards and when that happens, this game will have to be “retired” for a while.

Below is a sentence on the box top which provides a good, yet very simple, idea of what “brain games” are all about.
THINK YOU
YOU CAN'T
BE FOOLED?
You just were. Read it again.

If you did not find the double YOU in the phrase on the first try, then you were fooled.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX:
- 192 game cards consisting of 48 cards each in each of the 4 categories (mind & body, language, logic, vision)
- A "box topper" with 4 game slots to hold the cards
- 40 hexagon shaped game tiles (8 tiles for each category, 4 wild, and 4 lose-a-turn)
- 6 pawns (playing pieces)
- 6 score cards
- 1 game board in 4 puzzle pieces
- 1 die that holds numbers 1, 2, & 3 only (two times)

Everything is made of cardboard except for the pawns and die. The score cards and puzzle pieces are easily punched out of the cardboard card provided.

In summary, this game is good for those who like to be challenged or know what the game is about. However, if you play this several times, you'll probably remember the answers and have to put this away for about one year before playing it again.
text_fidelity_b: Brain Games - The Game - Based on the Emmy Nominated National Geographic Channel TV Series

LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces) I hope they don't overdo it, but this new LEGO Augmented Reality system is quite cool.

There is an app that you download to your phone, and using that app, you can view your LEGO set, and watch it move and change a little bit. If you've seen someone playing Pokemon Go or using a filter on their camera phone, you'll get the idea. It works surprisingly well given that it's easy to slightly alter the design. The app itself is downloadable on iTunes and Android, and works well on the Android system, although you really likely want to use a phone because of the size of the tablet. It will work, but it gets in the way of play.

Like all parents, I'm not entirely thrilled about yet another excuse to hand over my phone, but I think that the augmented reality piece is really more of a gimmick that my daughter will tire of sooner rather than later. The building of the set must come first in order for this to work, and that's mildly educational, and we get to play with the LEGO set without the phone as well.

And did I mention how cool this set is, even without the augmented reality? The ghost theme makes for some cool pieces, and I like how this one looks when it's done. It's a winner.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces)

Norberg & Linden Watercolor Paint Set - 36 Premium Paints - 12 Page Pad - 6 Brushes - Painting Supplies with Palette, Watercolors, Art Pad Paper and Artist Brushes Norberg & Linden LG40 Watercolor Paint Set is a great half pan set of 36 different colors. The set is in a metal tin with some wells in the lid, which can serve as a palette, it folds out on two hinges. A color chart is included along with a small pad of water color paper, a small brush and two pen brushes. The pen brushes will open to fill by turning the opposite direction than you may expect. I like to use distilled water with my watercolors, and strongly suggest everyone do this. It will keep fine in the refillable brush pens without allowing for microbial growth.

I really enjoyed this color palette because the colors are more natural, but still very vibrant. I found the colors to be very transparent, even yellow, which can pose an issue in similar sets. Blooming and blending were easy to achieve, allowing for a variety of effects. The binding agents are fair to good, as the pans were a little difficult to wet initally but soon took to the water very well.

This is a great set to gift as it includes brush pens, a brush and paper with the paint pans. This allows you to only add water to get started. I would not recommend this set for small children, and this is stated on the package. It contains small parts that may pose a choking hazard. This is a great budget set, a fair value and would be excellent for hobbyists and budding artists. I would not recommend it for professional artists, or upper-level students for course work, as this set is not designed for these users. I'm pleased with this set, and so would anyone else with an interest in watercolor painting. Thanks for reading, I hope this is Helpful to you, and you will click the button below.

text_fidelity_a: Magicfly Bingo Daubers, Washable Dot Markers, 8 Colors Non-Toxic Paint Daubers, Water-Based Dauber Markers These are the first dot markers my 3.5 year old and I have tried. She is really enjoying them, but they don’t work quite like I imagined or hoped. First, card stock or thick paper seems ideal for not letting the color bleed through, but since I didn’t have any on hand I had to stack 3 pieces of normal paper to keep the color off our table. Second, they take awhile to prime. Even a couple minutes of unuse will require you to hold the marker down extra long to get the ink back in the tip. Third, even after priming you cannot move quickly with these markers - you really need to patiently, slowly, and evenly push down each dot to get a full circle. Many of my daughters dots are incomplete and even when I tried I couldn’t consistently get a complete dot. Also some colors seem to work better than others. Overall my daughter still likes them, but I cannot see her using them that often or being pleased with the results as she gets older.
text_fidelity_b: Magicfly Bingo Daubers, Washable Dot Markers, 8 Colors Non-Toxic Paint Daubers, Water-Based Dauber Markers

Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit This THAMES & KOSMOS THE BIG ENGINEERING MAKERSPACE SCIENCE EXPERIMENT KIT is the real deal--a fun model-building kit that painlessly teaches basic concepts of physics (e.g., thermal air currents, levers, momentum). Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.

text_fidelity_a:
Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+ Initially I bought Snap-Circuits for my 4 and 5 year old boys. I found the collection of capacitors, resistors, integrated circuit modules, and transistors was a little too abstract, and I was thinking I really wanted more stuff like electro-magnets, relays, motors, generators, switches, potentiometers, and maybe resistive loads like light bulbs and diodes -- more basic electrical stuff, of which there's some in the circuit kits but not a lot.

My boys are 5 and 6 now. I added Snaptricity to our collection of mostly unexplored Snap-Circuits, and suddenly they're creating all kinds of basic circuits with switches, buttons, lights, motors, and electro-magnets. They're starting to understand the flow of electricity, polarity, magnetism, and resistance (as they add more loads to their circuits). I've set the transistors and stuff aside for now, because there's tons of stuff to do with these more basic components first. For older children, they might be ready for the electronic components sooner, but with my younger kids, these electrical parts are great.

We do not follow the instructions. So it helps to have extra components on hand instead of the minimum number required for the book experiments. Some of our circuits are more than elegant and minimalist. I recommend buying two kits, or this kit and another one like the 100 or 300.

The brilliant thing about these components is the incredibly simple and effective button snap-connectors. The only downside to these components is they are encased in plastic for durability. The plastic is clear so the internal components can be seen. This is really a good thing, but it's worthwhile to have a coil/electromagnet that is un-encased, as well as a speaker/microphone (electromagnet with a diaphragm) that is not encased, and a motor that can be disassembled/dissected.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do activities, and then the parent will secretly leave another activity in the fairy house. This is suppose to make the child believe the fairies left them a gift. (For example: The child is to craft 3 fairy bells and hang them around their room. Inside the fairy house, they'll place a stick, pebbles, and a leaf. They'll then spin the house and ring each bell to summon a fairy visit.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids. In my opinion, there's more in the wizard kit. There is the same amount of activities in both, but there's just not as much to do in this fairy kit. (It seems more stickers and easy crafts.) It's not high quality, but it's still nice enough. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there'd the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though the wizard kit that is similar to this one could work for boys and girls(and this one still could, if desired), this fairy kit is definitely targeted to girls. At the end, I couldn't help but feel sorry for all the little children doing these activities, hoping to see a fairy. While gifts are left, which are supposed to let the child know a fairy visited them, they'll never actually see one, unless the parent does something extra. We just did the crafts, since we don't do imaginary things as real. Without the added magical element, though, this kit just doesn't hold near as much value. If you're like us and don't do Santa and all, I'd recommend another kind of kit. If you do love the idea of pretending fairies are leaving gifts, this might be a blast for you and your child, as long as you don't think they'll be too disappointed that they never actually see a fairy. Overall, I found it a little disappointing, particularly considering the current price(which changes constantly).
text_fidelity_b: Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House

This set is for children age 3 and up because of small parts and a choking hazard.

Thank goodness my husband was able to grab it off of the porch before my daughter saw it and/or any porch pirates noticed it. I’d buy again. But clearly, there should have been better handling with the box!
